$comment: Short explanations for key repertoire decisions, keyed by the line before the move (SAN, space-separated), then by the move. Written for this project. Moves without a note get a generic explanation from src/trainer/explain.ts.

notes.e4: Open with 1.e4 at every level: take the center and free the queen and the light-squared bishop.

e4 e5.Nf3: Develop and attack e5 straight away.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6.Nc3: The simple system: both knights out, then the bishop, then castle.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6.Bc4: The bishop takes its most active diagonal, aiming at f7. Castle next.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6.d4: Hit the center while Black's pieces are still at home (the Scotch Four Knights).

e4 e5 Nf3 d6.Nc3: Keep developing: the system doesn't change against the Philidor.
e4 e5 Nf3 d6.d4: Against the Philidor, challenge e5 at once, before Black is set up.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6.Nc3: Defend e4 with a developing move and keep the game in familiar Four Knights shapes.

e4 c5.Nf3: Develop toward the center, the same knight move as against 1...e5.

e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6.Nc3: Stick to the system: second knight out, then the bishop and castle.
e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6.c3: The Alapin idea: prepare d4 so a pawn, not a piece, recaptures in the center.

e4 c5 Nf3 d6.c3: The Alapin idea: prepare d4 so a pawn, not a piece, recaptures in the center.

e4 c5 Nf3 e6.Nc3: Stick to the system: second knight out, then the bishop and castle.

e4 e6.Nf3: Develop and keep it simple; no French theory needed at this level.
e4 e6.d4: Take the full center. After ...d5, exchange on d5.

e4 e6 d4 d5.exd5: The Exchange French: an open, symmetrical position where quick development is easy.

e4 d5.exd5: Take the pawn: Black has to spend time winning it back.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5.Nc3: Develop with tempo: the knight attacks the queen.

e4 d5 exd5 Nf6.d4: Take the center while Black spends time regaining the pawn.

e4 c6.Nf3: Develop first; the set-up stays the same against the Caro-Kann.

e4 c6 Nf3 d5.exd5: Exchange to open the position for quick development.
e4 c6 Nf3 d5.Nc3: Defend e4 with a piece and keep the tension (the Two Knights).

e4.e5: Meet 1.e4 with 1...e5: an equal share of the center and open lines for the bishop and queen.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4.Bc5: Mirror White: the bishop goes to c5, aiming at f2.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4.exd4: Take the pawn. The center opens and your pieces come out quickly.

e4 e5 Qh5.Nc6: Defend e5 with a piece. Watch f7: if a bishop comes to c4, block with ...g6.

d4.d5: Meet 1.d4 with 1...d5: an equal share of the center.

d4 d5 c4.dxc4: Take the gambit pawn (Queen's Gambit Accepted), then develop quickly; don't cling to it.
d4 d5 c4.e6: The Queen's Gambit Declined: hold d5 with a pawn and develop behind it.

d4 d5 Bf4.Nf6: Against the London, develop the knight toward the center.
